title: U.S. House · California's 3rd District
area: Covers part of the Sierra Nevada foothills and Sacramento-area exurbs, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Ami Bera (D) placed first with 34.3% (76,653 votes) and Robb Tucker (R) placed second with 29.9% (66,808 votes) out of 223,711 total votes cast; both advanced to the general election.

candidates.name: Ami Bera
candidates.ballotNote: Placed first in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary

summary.text: Ami Bera is a Democratic physician who became a U.S. Representative from the Sacramento area in 2013 after serving as Sacramento County's Chief Medical Officer and a UC Davis School of Medicine administrator. He sits on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, where he is Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific, and on the House Intelligence Committee. His campaign materials emphasize health care, housing, jobs, Social Security and Medicare, and public safety.

background.text: Born March 2, 1965, in Los Angeles and raised in La Palma in Orange County, the son of Indian immigrants.
Attended California public schools through medical school, earning both a B.S. and an M.D. from UC Irvine; his official biography says he graduated from medical school in 1991.

Completed an internal medicine residency at California Pacific Medical Center, becoming chief resident, then practiced in the Sacramento area in leadership roles with MedClinic Medical Group and as medical director of care management for Mercy Healthcare.

Served as Sacramento County's Chief Medical Officer, then worked as clinical professor of medicine and associate dean for admissions and outreach at UC Davis; Wikipedia lists his clinical professorship as 2005 to 2012.
Challenged Republican Rep. Dan Lungren in 2010 and again in 2012; in 2012 he defeated Lungren in the newly redrawn 7th District by 3.4 points to win his first term.
Won re-election in 2014 by 0.8 points over Republican Doug Ose in a race Ballotpedia rated a battleground, and again in 2016 over Republican Scott Jones and in 2018 over Republican Andrew Grant.

Has represented Sacramento County in the House since January 2013. His official biography lists him as Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific, a member of the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and a member of the New Democrat Coalition; it describes him as the longest-serving Indian American in Congress.

His official biography says his office has helped return more than $23 million to local taxpayers and assisted more than 36,000 Sacramento County residents since 2013, and that he has lived in Sacramento County for over 30 years with his wife, Janine, a physician; they have a daughter, Sydra.

priorities.text: Supports universal coverage so every American has access to affordable, quality health care, and has worked to lower prescription drug and insulin costs.
Supports policies to increase housing supply and expand pathways to affordable homeownership in Sacramento County.
Says protecting Social Security and Medicare, including through the Social Security 2100 Act, is a priority for the region's seniors.

positions.summary: Says he supports universal health coverage so every American has access to affordable, quality health care.
positions.quote: That is why I support universal coverage so every American has access to affordable, quality health care.

positions.summary: Says he supports policies that increase housing supply and voted for the Housing for the 21st Century Act to expand housing supply and cut red tape on building.
positions.quote: That is why I support practical policies that increase housing supply, expand pathways to affordable homeownership, protect working families from being priced out by large institutional investors, and preserve existing affordable housing.

positions.summary: Says he has opposed sweeping tariff policies that raise costs for working families and small businesses.
positions.quote: I have also opposed sweeping tariff policies that raise costs for working families, hurt small businesses, and strain our economy.

positions.summary: Voted for the Women's Health Protection Act after the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade and for the Right to Contraception Act.
positions.quote: I voted for the Women’s Health Protection Act after the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, and I also voted for the Right to Contraception Act to protect access to birth control.

positions.summary: Says he voted for bipartisan legislation to increase funding for law enforcement and public safety programs, including officer recruitment and retention.
positions.quote: I voted for bipartisan legislation to increase funding for law enforcement and public safety programs, including support for officer recruitment and retention, homicide investigations, mental health first responder units, and evidence-based violence intervention programs.

record.text: Serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, including the National Intelligence Enterprise and National Security Agency and Cyber subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.
Serves on the House Committee on Foreign Affairs for the 2025-2026 session.
Reintroduced the bipartisan Improving Seniors' Timely Access to Care Act to reduce prior authorization delays in Medicare Advantage.

candidates.name: Robb Tucker
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: Member, Nevada County Board of Supervisors

summary.text: Robb Tucker is a Republican member of the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, elected in 2024, and a former president and CEO of a family business that owned a mobile home community. According to his campaign, he was raised in southern Nevada County and holds degrees from Pepperdine University and Wheaton College Graduate School. He is running on local control, public safety, small business and fiscal discipline.

background.text: According to his campaign website, was born and raised in Nevada County and he and his wife are raising their children there; his campaign says he is the grandson and son of retired U.S. Air Force pilots.
According to his campaign, earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Pepperdine University and a master's degree from Wheaton College Graduate School.
According to his campaign, served as president and CEO of a closely held family business that owned the Forest Springs Mobilehome Community until selling the business in 2020.

Elected to the Nevada County Board of Supervisors in 2024; his campaign says he has focused on public safety, support for small businesses and jobs, and a balance of growth, development and agriculture.

Serves on the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, where his campaign says he has worked to secure funding for shelters, mental health care, and public safety equipment despite mismatched state and federal funding streams.

According to his campaign, he holds a commercial pilot license with multi-engine and instrument ratings, has coached youth and prep sports for decades, is active in local schools and his church, and lives in South Nevada County with his wife, Kristy, and their three children.

Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary to the November 3 general election as a Republican candidate for California's 3rd District; he has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

priorities.text: Campaign platform centers on 'local control and federal accountability,' arguing federal agencies should consult counties before making major land, water, or infrastructure decisions and should simplify compliance rules for rural jurisdictions.
priorities.quote: Washington has treated Northern California's rural counties as an afterthought for too long. Federal agencies write regulations for Los Angeles and San Francisco, then hand them down to communities that operate nothing like a major metro area.

positions.summary: Platform lists securing the border as a core federal duty and says Washington's failure to do so burdens local law enforcement.
positions.quote: Every time Washington fails to secure the border or coordinate offender releases, local deputies absorb the burden.

positions.summary: Says the federal government should direct more funding toward tools used by local law enforcement, such as radios, vehicles, and forensic equipment.
positions.quote: Robb wants federal dollars going to the tools deputies actually use, like radios, vehicles, and forensic equipment, instead of sitting in Washington bureaucracy.

record.text: As a Nevada County Supervisor, voted to approve inter-agency contracts and emergency plans intended to streamline local operational agreements, according to his campaign.
As a Nevada County Supervisor, voted to fund sheriff communications and mobile technology upgrades, according to his campaign.

researchNotes: Neither candidate has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Bera's priorities and issue positions were drawn from his official House issues pages; his committee roles and a sponsored bill are listed as record. Tucker's positions and county-board record items are drawn from claims on his own campaign website, which were not independently verified against county meeting records. Biography gaps: Bera's biography comes from his official House page (which still describes the pre-redistricting 6th District) and Wikipedia; Tucker's biography is drawn from his campaign site and a campaign-submitted article in The Union, and his education, family-business and pilot details are self-reported and not independently verified.
